title: How Web Summit's Day 2 was called off
standfirst: 19:09 on Tuesday, and what led to it: a red warning before breakfast, a minister who said the venue was indoors, a mayor who said it could not run, water in a pavilion, a recommendation, and then a page on a path we were not watching.

warnings_in_force.about: The official warnings a story about the storm states first: resolved from IPMA's open data in the data room when the page is built, and read again in the reader's browser.

sections.title: Tuesday morning: the warning, and "um local fechado"
Tuesday afternoon: the mayor, the water, the recommendation

claims.text: At 07:18 on Tuesday IPMA sent the red wind warning for Lisbon, for Wednesday 12:00 to 21:00: the hours of Web Summit's second day.
claims.label: fact

claims.text: At 09:30 the Interior Minister, asked at the press conference that announced the alert situation, said "a Web Summit é um local fechado": if the organisers decided to keep the event, they could.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: the Interior Minister, as reported by Observador's live blog

claims.text: At 12:45 the organisers were reported as following the alerts with ANEPC and PSP, with no sign of cancelling Wednesday.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Web Summit's organisers, as reported by Jornal de Negócios' live blog

claims.text: At 13:19 Lisbon's mayor said "Tudo indica que a Web Summit não poderá funcionar amanhã", and that the decision was the Interior Ministry's and the organisers'.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: Lisbon's mayor, as reported by Jornal Económico

claims.text: Through the afternoon the storm was already at the venue, by the press's account: a thin audience at 15:19; at 17:07, water entering a pavilion between halls 4 and 5 and participants leaving early.
claims.label: evidence

claims.text: At 17:53 the government's position had changed: it recommended suspending Web Summit on Wednesday ("Já emitimos a nossa recomendação de que os trabalhos desse evento possam suspender-se"), and left the decision with the organisers. That is 8 hours 23 minutes after the minister's "local fechado".
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: the Government, as reported by Jornal de Negócios' live blog (no government page was found)

contains: Já emitimos a nossa recomendação de que os trabalhos desse evento possam suspender-se

claims.text: For more than an hour nothing came from the organisers: no statement at 18:25, none at 18:53, and at 19:05 no decision on their home page, news list, sitemap or official Bluesky.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: this site's desks, reading Web Summit's channels (the 18:25 and 18:53 reads are of press pages: evidence)

claims.text: At 19:09 Web Summit published "Important event update": "Web Summit will of course respect the Government's direction, and accordingly, Day 2 (Wednesday, November 11th) will not take place." Its reasons: tidal flooding, disruption to public transport, high winds on external structures.
claims.label: fact

contains: Web Summit will of course respect the Government's direction, and accordingly, Day 2 (Wednesday, November 11th) will not take place.

claims.text: The page went up under /blog/web-summit/, which is not in the site's news list or its sitemap. Attendees were told by email at 19:38, as relayed to us; the press had it from 19:41.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: this site's record of where the notice was (the email and the press times are evidence)

claims.text: We missed it for an hour and three quarters. At 19:52 the lead checked websummit.com's home and news list and found no notice; the page had been up since 19:09 on a path we did not watch, and was read at source at 20:58.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: incident.conductor@web-summit.dinis, in the timeline, and incident.researcher@'s lesson in the decision graph

claims.text: On Thursday the organisers' own words are an aim: "Web Summit aims to proceed with Day 3 (Thursday, November 12) as planned, following the passing of Storm Charles". The press rendered it three ways: "conforme planeado" (RTP), "if the weather allows" (Diário de Notícias), and the page's own "aims to proceed".
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: Web Summit, "Important event update" (the renderings are evidence: RTP, Diário de Notícias)

contains: an aim, not yet a promise

claims.text: The post was modified at 20:06 with its text on Day 2 and Day 3 unchanged, and by 21:53 there was no further statement. Still unannounced then: what happens to Wednesday's talks, the PITCH semi-final, side events and tickets.
claims.label: fact
claims.said_by: Web Summit's blog listing, as watched; this site's desks

claims.text: Set in order: red wind warning 07:18; "local fechado" 09:30; the mayor 13:19; water in a pavilion 17:07; the government's recommendation 17:53; the organisers' page 19:09, 76 minutes after the recommendation and 11 hours 50 minutes after the warning.
claims.label: evidence
claims.said_by: this desk, subtracting the times in the sentences it names

not_known.text: What passed between the government, ANEPC, PSP and the organisers, and when: the organisers' page speaks of the government's "direction"; the only time we have for the recommendation is the first press report, 17:53.

Why the minister's position at 09:30 and the government's at 17:53 differ: no source in the data room says. The red rain warning (sent 16:30) and the water at the venue (17:07) fall between them; nothing here says either was the reason.
What happens to Wednesday's talks, the PITCH semi-final, side events and tickets: unannounced at our last read.
Whether Day 3 runs: the organisers' word is "aims". For that, the page itself and IPMA's warnings for Thursday.
The email to attendees has no public address: it is in this story only as relayed (evidence), at 19:38.
